summary: Streaming panel: enabling response compression (gzip) causes live panels to lose trace headers and break alert trace links
description:
Issue summary: Customers using the Console live/streaming panel reported that when the "console setting" to compress streaming responses (gzip) is enabled, trace context headers (X-Trace-Id / X-Trace-Span) are not preserved or become unrecognizable by the dashboard link parser.

Impact: Live streaming widgets show event text but the "View trace" links disappear or open a 404 in trace explorer. Alerts that rely on trace anchors from streaming events do not link to the correct trace. Affects monitoring and incident triage for customers using streaming trace hooks.

Environment: Production, us-east-1. Reported by Nimbus AI (enterprise) on multiple orgs using Console live panels connected to long-running streaming endpoints (SSE / chunked responses) with per-event tracing headers supplied by the tracing-hook.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a live streaming panel in Console pointed at an SSE endpoint that emits per-event tracing headers (X-Trace-Id) in the preamble.
2) Make sure the Console user setting 'Compress streaming responses (gzip)' is toggled ON (Account > Preferences > Streaming).
3) Produce streaming events where a single event payload crosses ~8KB (easily reproduced with a long embedding or debug dump).
4) Observe the live panel: events render but the 'Trace link' icon is missing for affected events.
5) Open network tab -> inspect SSE chunks; compare header presence when compression is ON vs OFF.
observed_behavior:
With compression enabled, the proxied streaming responses still arrive but the tracing headers are missing from the parsed event metadata. Dashboard no longer displays trace anchors; alert links originating from those events fail to open the matching trace or show 'trace not found'.

Server-side logs show the request to /streaming/proxy completed with 200 and chunked transfer, but tracing header fields are not seen by the Console parser when compression is active.
expected_behavior: Even when response compression is enabled, the Console should preserve per-event tracing metadata and expose trace links for each streaming event. Enabling gzip must not alter or drop X-Trace-* headers or otherwise change how the tracing-hook attaches metadata to events.

comments: 2024-11-20 09:25 - Maya R. Collins (Support): Acknowledged. Reproduced on a Nimbus prod org. Added to priority queue and requested SRE assistance. Asked customer for the panel ID and recent request_id values.

2024-11-20 10:02 - Ethan J. Park (SRE): I can reproduce on staging when streaming events exceed ~8KB and proxy buffering triggers. Hypothesis: ngx_http_gzip_module or proxy_buffering is interacting with our SSE header passthrough and moving header bytes into the compressed chunk body, causing the Console parser — which expects headers in the SSE preamble — to miss them.
Filed an engineering task and started a local repro with nginx config toggles.

2024-11-21 07:30 - Priya K. Sharma (Infra Eng): Confirmed: compression combined with proxy_buffering causes headers to be rewritten in a way that the SSE preamble parser doesn't see. We have a branch to add 'proxy_buffering off' for /streaming/proxy endpoints and to mark responses as 'not gzip' for SSE. Preparing PR for hotfix.
investigation_notes:
- Repro steps validated on staging and prod with controlled SSE generator.
- Root cause: nginx gzip filter and proxy_buffering buffer thresholds compress the first X bytes of the chunked stream; header-like prefix that carries X-Trace-* can end up merged/encoded in body, Console SSE parser (which expects plain header lines before event data) fails to extract trace headers.
- Regression window: introduced after nginx config change in release 2024-11-05 that enabled gzip for proxy routes to save bandwidth.
- Affected traffic: streaming endpoints that use per-event tracing headers and produce event sizes > 8KB. Short events unaffected.
resolution:
Workaround: temporarily disable 'Compress streaming responses (gzip)' in Console user preferences for affected orgs OR set 'proxy_buffering off' for affected upstream in the edge proxy.
Fix: merged hotfix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218 to set proxy_buffering off for streaming proxy and to ensure our console client does not request gzip for SSE endpoints. Hotfix deployed to us-east-1 on 2024-11-21 03:12 UTC.
Follow-ups: Add e2e tests for SSE + compression in CI, update runbook to avoid enabling gzip on streaming routes, add a console warning in preferences when toggling compression for orgs with active streaming trace hooks.
Status: Hotfix deployed and verified on Nimbus prod org; monitoring for related incidents for 48 hours.
resolution_notes: 2024-11-21 04:00 - Ethan J. Park (SRE): Hotfix rolled to prod in us-east-1. Verified trace links restored for events >8KB. Customer confirmed fix: Nimbus reported trace icons reappeared in their live panel and alerts now link correctly. Follow-up ticket opened to add CI test coverage.
customer_follow_up: 2024-11-21 08:14 - Nimbus AI (customer): Confirmed resolution, thanks. Please advise when permanent fix and CI coverage are in place. Asked for confirmation the toggle will not reintroduce the issue if re-enabled by mistake.
next_steps: 1) Add CI test for SSE event sizes with compression enabled and ensure parsing retains headers. 2) Update edge proxy defaults to keep proxy_buffering off for streaming endpoints. 3) Add Console UI guardrail: present warning when enabling compression for orgs with active tracing hooks. 4) Close follow-up support ticket after 48h of monitoring.
